encoding.objects: All listed fields required; unknown fields, duplicate JSON keys, non-finite numbers and invalid UTF-8 rejected. No normalization of opaque identities.
encoding.integers: All wire counts, generations, offsets and revisions are canonical unsigned decimal strings, no leading zero except 0. UInt64 maximum. Server-generated SQLite revisions/generations are bounded to Int64 maximum and fail before exhaustion.
encoding.opaque_id: Nonempty UTF-8 string, at most 1024 UTF-8 bytes, no NUL. Used unchanged. Only server-generated artifact IDs become filenames. Opaque distribution/transport/attempt IDs in HTTP headers use canonical base64url of UTF-8 without padding; response Distribution-ID uses that same encoding. UUID rendition IDs and decimal generation/hash headers are literal ASCII.
encoding.range: Half-open [lower_bound, upper_bound); HTTP Range is bytes=lower_bound-(upper_bound-1). Full requests have range=null. Multiple/suffix/open-ended ranges rejected.
encoding.receipt: Explicit schema mapped into Swift values after exact identity/revision validation; not synthesized Swift enum Codable. A receipt is a historical commit, never a lasting GET permission.
encoding.response_bound: Publication client maximum 262144 bytes (256KiB); invalidation endpoint emits at most 196608 UTF-8 encoded bytes. A single worst-case escaped invalidation (bounded opaque fields plus server UUIDs/decimal counters) fits; oversize first items fail explicitly rather than return a nonprogressing page.

rendition.rendition_id: Server-generated canonical lowercase hyphenated UUID; this is not a constraint on all Domain opaque IDs

types.media_type: video/mp4 or video/quicktime; verified artifact container, not S26 output selection or codec/quality acceptance

result.media_type: media_type when current exists, otherwise null

endpoints.effect: Read only. Does not add a recipient or construct a distribution receipt.

result.media_type: media_type of this exact immutable rendition

endpoints.effect: source requires kind=full, range=null, source_operation_id=null; commits the first receipt before RetrieveMediaCommand exists. read references a committed source for the same rendition/registration/gate and uses a fresh operation for each actual GET. Required recipients are committed with either acceptance. Exact replay returns the same receipt; changed payload is conflict.

result.original_request: Exact accepted request, not lookup request

endpoints.effect: Envelope request echoes the lookup request. ACK operation_id equals acknowledgement.invalidation.invalidation_id; lookup uniqueness is kind=acknowledgement plus registration. No additional ACK operation is invented. Missing operation is 404 publication_operation_not_executed.

headers.Range: Exact single range, absent only for kind=full

endpoints.response: 200 full or 206 exact range; Content-Type equals persisted artifact media_type and manifest/distribution media_type; Content-Length and Content-Range for 206; no transformation; Cache-Control no-store
endpoints.effect: Open/read/hash same FD outside writer, then recheck exact request, current publication, registration, invalidation, artifact and authority in a short transaction; consume ticket once and commit admission before any bytes. Reused ticket including URLSession internal replay is 409 with zero media bytes. Lost/partial response requires a new read distribution and all checks again; no automatic retry in the transport adapter.

Sync an existing local explicit-user confirmation commit; do not create confirmation from server byte counts or status sync. Require exact source receipt and current, noninvalidated rendition. Historical replay does not restore current validity.

Read only; each pending replacement derives required registrations from all recipients of previous rendition, including recipients added while waiting. Binary invalidation_id keyset order, strictly after cursor. Each poll starts with null. Count is at most limit and complete UTF-8 JSON envelope is at most 196608 bytes (192KiB). A short page can have next_after; continue whenever nonnull. Empty page always has null cursor. Server sends the exact bytes used for this bound. Concurrent lower-ID additions are found by the next poll from null. Page completion never means all ACKs.

Require matching existing invalidation/recipient/registration and local tombstone commit receipt. Local all-reader stop/release precedes this outbox delivery. New registrations never replace old ACKs. Same acknowledgement replay is stable; different local receipt/payload rejected. Lookup operation_id is invalidation.invalidation_id, scoped by registration; original_request/original_result are returned unchanged.

http_errors.409: exact payload conflict, stale publication/revision, invalidated, consumed ticket or awaiting ACK
http_errors.503: database/file unavailable, production proof not implemented or result unknown

sqlite.initial: current=NULL; no fabricated previous rendition or ACK. Artifact/pointer/receipt commit together with expected revision.
sqlite.replacement: Keep V1 pointer. Required set is all immutable recipients of V1. New distribution adds recipient in same commit. Final publication rechecks exact candidate/revision/all required ACKs in one transaction. No timeout, old-registration replacement or legacy pointer update.
sqlite.identity: candidate generation, publication generation, invalidation generation, revision and transport attempt are distinct; typed operation identity plus full canonical payload must match on replay. Registered operations use (kind, registration_id, operation_id); GET admissions use (registration_id, distribution_operation_id). Internal publication operations have empty registration scope. Equal opaque operation IDs in different registrations do not interfere.
sqlite.confirmation: Retain exact local record in operation ledger; server acceptance and currently valid confirmation are different observations. Never reinterpret local revision as publication revision.

authority_boundary.production: ProductionPublicationAuthority unconditionally reports publication_proof_not_implemented until S26 formal proof/validator is connected. candidate_ready, is_log=0 or boolean edits cannot authorize publication or reads. Every artifact read is authority checked, including an existing fixture-populated DB.
authority_boundary.test: Only a tests-owned factory explicitly supplies FixturePublicationAuthority. Persist proof_kind=technical_fixture and complete fixture provenance. No environment switch, production API or default factory accepts it.
authority_boundary.real_wire_test: Use the same fr-publication-v1 wire and real iOS codec. The separately reviewed fixture listener is loopback-only, uses disposable DB/media and independent secret, and records fixture authority/source identities in its evidence. Canonical wire success is publication-order/transport evidence, not Rec.709 or product-quality success. Production routers never construct the fixture authority.

artifact_boundary: Copy candidate into a distinct inode, create-only sealed server-named path; close every writer, fsync and independently reread. App writers cannot replace/write/alias/reclaim sealed artifacts. Keep one read FD across whole hash, short admission commit and streaming. Metadata/permission/same-FD do not prevent arbitrary external in-place writes: reject detected pre-send changes and abort on detected later changes without claiming already-sent bytes retractable. Artifact filenames use server UUID.media and do not claim a container. Container media_type is independently checked from the sealed FD; technical fixture HTTP uses real QuickTime/PCM.
open_items: S26 production proof schema/validator remains unimplemented and denies access
Test factory/listener exact ownership and isolation must be reviewed before execution
